about: The first of the two prayers at the ablutions, said while the minister pours wine into the chalice. It asks that what has passed the lips be taken up with a pure heart, and that a gift given in time become an everlasting remedy.

s02.translation: Lord, may we receive with a pure heart what our mouths have received, and may the gift given in time become for us an everlasting remedy.

s03.narrative: Meanwhile the priest holds out the chalice to the server, who pours a little wine into it, and with this the priest purifies himself.

w001.explanation: Latin can leave the antecedent unsaid where English needs a word for it.

w006.explanation: The translation renders this interior disposition as “purity of heart”.

w007.explanation: The prayer asks that what has been received by mouth also be received with a pure mind.
